issue_context.title: kubectl: Azure AAD authentication should handle refresh token timeout
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

Currently, when AAD login is configured, refresh token timeout would make kubectl print an error, not able to re-login without manually remove the tokens. Expect kubectl to promote user to login again.

**Why is this needed**:

Configure refresh-token timeout from Azure is a way to force re-login after inactivity. kubectl doesn't promote re-login makes users harder to apply timeout policy.

the root cause of this issue is in this [file](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3e60b6e1c7bc147740800b7ac52712d55579844/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/plugin/pkg/client/auth/azure/azure.go#L178)
1. it first gets the cached token (result of device code flow) at [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3e60b6e1c7bc147740800b7ac52712d55579844/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/plugin/pkg/client/auth/azure/azure.go#L183)
1. then it's trying to refresh an expired token at [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3e60b6e1c7bc147740800b7ac52712d55579844/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/plugin/pkg/client/auth/azure/azure.go#L201) and failed. An error is returned.

Since the expired token is still in the cache, it will always hit this path until user removes the token from kubeconfig.

the fix should be:
1. remove the token from cache
1. do a retry to re-initiate the device code flow in [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3e60b6e1c7bc147740800b7ac52712d55579844/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/plugin/pkg/client/auth/azure/azure.go#L187)

review_comments: What happens if err is not nil AND token is not nil? Previously, the non-nil error ruled. With this PR, the token value is later inspected/used if non-nil, even in error cases.

this assumes a nil token object is returned in error cases... it is more accepted to use a non-nil error to decide whether an error handling path should be taken (alternatively, only assign to `token` in non-error cases)
